owner: Hypersolve ordered-field root isolation, existing Sturm distinct-root counts and selected polynomial fields. Hypercurve geometric construction is a later consumer.
domain: Finite univariate polynomials over an admitted exact ordered selected field, in a finite closed represented interval. Arbitrary finite degrees, algebraic coefficients, reducible/repeated polynomials, exact boundary/midpoint roots and multiple separated roots. Original equations, selectors and shared coefficient dependencies must survive selection and replay.
baseline: controls/selected-field-root-discovery-frontier1, source-attributed existing public API probe; simple t^3-a and repeated (t^3-a)^2 with a^3=2 fail discovery. The original elliptic contact succeeds and must remain supported.
planned_route: Keep the existing bounded Bernstein filter and its documented fallback behavior. Add a complete ordered-field route reusing authoritative Sturm counts and existing field operations. A selected-field entry point lifts coefficients, runs a strict complete discovery and consumes singleton intervals into ordinary retained values; use original equations for nonpoint selections.
isolation_invariants: Never emit a partial root list as completed output.
Partition intervals only with certified signs/counts. Nonpoint selectors must exclude original roots at their endpoints, including separately emitted exact roots.
Use strict field signs for represented interval order; maintain output order by the certified subdivision traversal, not approximate sorting.
Repeated factors keep their original equation; distinct-root isolation must not claim to discard their multiplicity.
When a dyadic midpoint is a root, certify a root-free gap on each side before recursing; endpoint roots require analogous exclusion using existing exact deflation and original guards.

Every subdivision/refinement consumes the existing shared root-refinement work unit. Zero/invalid/no-root outcomes remain distinct; a denied actual unit produces typed exhaustion and clears provisional intervals.
implementation_constraints: No second field/sign/root-count authority, independent scalar projection, tolerance, degree cap presented as completeness, artificial charges or weakened original fixtures. Existing bounded API behavior remains intact. Root discovery and geometric consumption are separate claims.
acceptance: Nested simple and repeated fields; multiple roots with independently known factors; nonmonic and zero leading coefficients; rational boundary and midpoint roots.
2^-160-separated distinct roots, exact root/selector relations, rootlessness and zero equation.
Select discovered roots in their original coefficient fields, query and join them, save/replay defining graph, then perform another field operation.
Small shared budgets and repeated larger retry; no partial success or poisoned cache.
Original elliptic contact discovery/control preserved with original curve, radius and side assertions.
resource_limits: Shared refinement/promotion counters do not bound total arithmetic, coefficient/expression growth, memory, cancellation or wall time. The complete route has no promised uniform practical bound; lower context undecidability and configured work refusals remain explicit. Ordinary completed fixtures and stress/refusal observations must be separate.
status: Fresh target baseline reproduced all three outcomes; implementation now adds a separate complete ordered-field isolation API. Selected-field consumers retain the original equation and select each resulting interval through the existing API. A convenience field wrapper is deferred.
interval_precondition: As in the existing Bernstein API, the closed search interval must have lower < upper. Zero-width and reversed ranges are explicitly invalid; the corpus already asserts both. Exact endpoint roots remain admitted and are emitted as selected point intervals.
